topic: Analyzing traffic discrepancies and frequency formulas
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on discrepancies in traffic data observed between the production and staging environments, particularly concerning unique counts (uniques) and total traffic calculations. Initial observations noted that external data sources showed significantly lower unique visitor counts compared to internal metrics.

A core technical issue identified was a potential double application of frequency formulas when calculating Total Traffic for malls/parks using cluster factors. Specifically, the standard frequency calculation appeared to be applied twice—once normally, and again relative to 'cluster' sessions (2- or 8-hour intervals)—leading to an underestimation of the true Total Traffic.

Multiple data points were compared for a specific location (Santo Amaro), showing significant differences between calculated totals when standard frequency was removed versus when it was included. The conversation concluded with comparing an internal formula's output (7.79) against an external benchmark (7.3) using the entire Brazilian market as a single facility.
decisions: A follow-up call is needed to resolve discrepancies in traffic calculations and frequency formulas.
action_items: Investigate why standard frequency calculation might be double-applied when calculating Total Traffic for malls/parks using cluster factors.
